items.stem: With the help of an appropriate example, justify that some of the chemical reactions are determined by (a) Change in temperature, (b) Evolution of a gas, and (c) Change in colour. Give chemical equation for the reaction involved in each case.
items.answer:
(a) Change in temperature: When zinc reacts with sulphuric acid, the test tube in which the reaction is taking place will be hot, indicating that the temperature is rising during the reaction.
Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(s) + H₂(g)
(b) Evolution of a gas: The chemical reaction between zinc and dilute sulphuric acid is characterized by the evolution of hydrogen gas. On bringing a burning matchstick near the gas jar, if it burns with a pop sound, the presence of hydrogen gas is confirmed.
Zn(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(s) + H₂(g)
(c) Change in colour: The reaction between lead nitrate solution and potassium iodide solution. In this reaction colour changes from colourless to yellow.
Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq)

items.stem: (a) Design an activity to demonstrate the decomposition reaction of lead nitrate. (b) Draw labelled diagram of the experimental setup. List two main observations. Write balanced chemical equation for the reaction stating the physical state of the reactants and the products.
items.answer:
(a) Take a small amount of lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube. Hold the boiling tube with a pair of tongs and heat it over the flame first gently and then strongly.
(b) Labelled diagram of the experimental setup: a boiling tube of lead nitrate powder held with tongs over a burner flame, with the brown fumes escaping from the mouth of the tube labelled.
Two main observations:
(i) We observe emission of brown fumes of a gas which is nitrogen dioxide.
(ii) The white colour of lead nitrate changes to yellow colour as lead oxide is formed.
(c) Balanced equation: 2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)

items.stem: What is observed after about 1 hour of adding the strips of copper and aluminium separately to ferrous sulphate solution filled in two beakers? Name the reaction if any change in colour is noticed. Also, write chemical equation for the reaction.
items.answer:
When a strip of copper is added to ferrous sulphate solution taken in a beaker, no change is observed (copper is less reactive than iron and cannot displace it).
On adding a strip of aluminium to ferrous sulphate solution taken in another beaker, we observe that the greenish colour of ferrous sulphate solution starts fading and it becomes colourless after about an hour.
The reaction taking place is a displacement reaction.
Equation of the reaction taking place:
2Al + 3FeSO₄ → 3Fe + Al₂(SO₄)₃

items.stem: A student wants to study a decomposition reaction by taking ferrous sulphate crystals. Write two precautions he must observe while performing the experiment.
items.answer:
Precautions to be observed for studying the decomposition reaction:
(a) Use only a hard boiling test tube.
(b) Hold the test tube in an inclined position away from your body and do not point the mouth of the boiling tube at your neighbours or yourself.
(c) Use a pair of tongs for holding the boiling tube while heating and don't touch the boiling tube with your bare hands.
(d) Do not inhale the gases emitted directly; they should be inhaled by wafting gently towards your nose.
items.ocr: The question asks for two precautions but the printed answer key lists four; all four are kept. 'Use a pair to tongs' read as 'a pair of tongs'.

items.stem: How is a chemical equation written? Illustrate with an example.
items.answer:
Let it be required to write a chemical equation that describes the reaction between magnesium and sulphuric acid to produce magnesium sulphate and hydrogen.
(i) Write the symbols of all the substances involved in the reaction — first the reactants and then the products — one after the other, on the same line.
Reactants: Mg   H₂SO₄      Products: MgSO₄   H₂
(ii) Separate the reacting substances from the products by a symbol meaning "produce". The sign → (an arrow), or sometimes the sign =, is used for this purpose.
Mg   H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄   H₂
(iii) Then put a + sign between the reactants indicating that these 'react', and a + sign between the products which signifies 'and'.
Mg + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂

items.stem: Describe the method of balancing a chemical equation.
items.answer:
The following sequential steps should be taken to obtain a balanced chemical equation: (i) First the skeleton equation is written. For example, H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (ii) The same total of charges should appear on the left and right side of the equation. (iii) Now one of the atoms is made equal on both sides by multiplying a molecule or compound with an integral number so that the desired element is balanced. It is convenient to start with the molecule or compound that contains the maximum number of atoms. Here, H₂O contains the maximum number of atoms. It is one short of an oxygen atom and so it is multiplied by 2: H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (iv) Next, the effect of multiplication of the molecule on the balance of other atoms is examined. As is seen, the number of oxygen atoms on both sides balances but now the number of hydrogen atoms on the left is 2 less. So, multiply H₂ on the left by 2: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (v) Further, count the number of atoms of each type on both sides.
AtomOn rightOn left
H44
022
Now, the equation is balanced. If the number of atoms on both sides do not agree, the above steps should be continued till a balanced equation is obtained. This is called the hit and trial method. If the reaction is complicated, i.e., it involves a large number of reactants and products, it is preferred to write the equation in steps (the actual reaction may or may not take place in these steps). For example, when copper reacts with conc. nitric acid, the products are copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide and water. Cu + HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + NO₂ + H₂O We can write this reaction in three steps and balance each step separately. (i) First, HNO₃ is decomposed to give nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), water (H₂O) and atomic oxygen. 2HNO₃ → 2NO₂ + H₂O + O ...(1) (ii) In the next step, copper is oxidised to copper(II) oxide (CuO). Cu + O → CuO ...(2) (iii) Copper oxide so formed then reacts with nitric acid to form copper nitrate, Cu(NO₃)₂, and water. CuO + 2HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + H₂O ...(3) Next, eq. (1), (2), (3) are multiplied by an integer so that on adding (1), (2) and (3), the intermediate products (which do not appear in the final reaction) cancel out. In this case we find that the integer is one. So (1), (2) and (3) are added and the final balanced equation is written as below: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O This method is known as the partial equation method.

items.stem: What are the drawbacks of a chemical equation? Illustrate with an example.
items.answer:
A balanced chemical equation does not give the following information:
(i) The physical state of the reactants and products — whether these are solids, liquids or gases, etc.
(ii) Concentration of reactants and products.
(iii) Conditions of reaction such as temperature, pressure, catalyst and light.
(iv) The rate of reaction — whether it is slow or fast.
(v) Time taken for completion of the reaction.
(vi) Heat changes — whether heat is evolved or absorbed.
(vii) Whether the reaction is reversible or irreversible.

items.stem: How can a chemical reaction be made more informative?
items.answer:
(i) The physical condition of the various species may be indicated by the signs (s), (l) and (g) for solid, liquid and gas respectively after the formula of a substance, e.g.,
2P(s) + 3Cl₂(g) → 2PCl₃(l)
(ii) The precipitate formed in the reaction is shown by an arrow pointing downward (↓), e.g.,
BaCl₂ + H₂SO₄ → BaSO₄↓ + 2HCl
(iii) An arrow pointing upward (↑) is used for a gas evolved.
Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂↑
(iv) If a substance dissolved in water is used or produced, the sign (aq) is used.
NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O
(v) Heat changes occurring during a chemical reaction may also be indicated, such as
2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l)   ΔH = +571.6 kJ  [Endothermic reaction]
H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g)   ΔH = −184.7 kJ
items.ocr: MinerU lost the upward-arrow glyph in step (iii), printing '(- sign is used for gas evolved'; restored from the equation on the next line, which does print H₂↑. The printed equation in (iii), Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂↑, is unbalanced in the book (it needs 2HCl); reproduced as printed. The printed heat-change example gives ΔH = +571.6 kJ and labels the formation of water endothermic, which is wrong — that reaction is exothermic — but it is reproduced as printed.

items.stem: Define the terms: (i) Oxidising agent and (ii) Reducing agent.
items.answer:
(i) Oxidising agent: It is the substance which in a reaction (a) gives up oxygen or any electronegative element, or (b) accepts hydrogen or any electropositive element, or (c) accepts electrons.
(ii) Reducing agent: It is the substance which in a reaction (a) gives up hydrogen or any electropositive element, or (b) accepts oxygen or any electronegative element, or (c) releases electrons.
In the following reaction:
H₂S + Cl₂ → S + 2HCl
Chlorine accepts hydrogen from H₂S, thus oxidising it, and is called the oxidising agent.
In a chemical reaction, the oxidising agent is reduced and the reducing agent is oxidised. In the reaction between zinc and copper sulphate solution:
Zn + Cu²⁺SO₄²⁻ → Zn²⁺SO₄²⁻ + Cu
Zn reduces Cu²⁺ to Cu, itself being oxidised to Zn²⁺, so Zn acts as a reducing agent.

items.answer:

CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq)
(quick lime)      (slaked lime)
(b) MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂
(c) A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products is known as a decomposition reaction.
Example: CaCO₃(s) --Heat--> CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
(calcium carbonate)

items.stem:
When a green salt is heated strongly, its colour finally changes to brown and the odour of burning sulphur is given out.
(a) Name the iron salt and write its formula.
(b) Name the brown substance obtained and write its formula.
(c) Which product gives the odour of burning sulphur? Write the formula.
(d) Write the chemical equation of the reaction involved.
(e) Name the type of chemical reaction which takes place during the heating of the iron salt.
items.answer:
(a) Ferrous sulphate, FeSO₄
(b) Ferric oxide, Fe₂O₃
(c) Sulphur dioxide, SO₂
(d) 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)
    (ferrous sulphate → ferric oxide + sulphur dioxide + sulphur trioxide)
(e) Decomposition reaction.

items.stem:
(a) Define corrosion.
(b) What is the name given to the corrosion of iron?
(c) What is the colour of the coating formed on silver and copper?
(d) What damage is caused by corrosion?
(e) How can we prevent corrosion?
items.answer:
(a) The surface of a metal reacts with atmospheric oxygen, moisture and carbon dioxide to form a coating on the surface. This phenomenon is called corrosion.
(b) When the metal involved is iron, the phenomenon of corrosion is called rusting.
(c) Silver forms a black coating and copper forms a green coating on the surface when exposed to the atmosphere for a long time.
(d) Corrosion weakens the metal. A great deal of damage is caused to car bodies, bridges, iron railings and ships.
(e) Corrosion can be prevented by coating the metal surface with paint.
items.ocr: The printed answer key omits the labels '(c)' and '(e)'; the sentence about the black and green coatings answers (c) and the closing sentence about painting answers (e), so the labels have been restored. 'When the metal involved in iron' read as 'is iron'.

items.stem:
(i) Name two effects of oxidation in daily life.
(ii) Why do iron articles become brown after some time?
(iii) Define the term corrosion. Give an example of corrosion.
(iv) Give the conditions of corrosion.
(v) What is rancidity?
items.answer:
(i) Corrosion and rancidity.
(ii) Due to corrosion (rusting of iron).
(iii) The process in which metals are eaten up gradually by the action of air, moisture or a chemical (such as an acid) on their surface is called corrosion. Example: the rusting of iron.
(iv) (a) Presence of moisture. (b) Presence of air (oxygen).
(v) Rancidity: When fats and oils are oxidised (or kept in the open for some days), their smell and taste change. We say that they have gone rancid. The condition produced by aerial oxidation of fats and oils in foods, marked by an unpleasant smell and taste, is called rancidity. Rancidity spoils food materials prepared in fats and oils which have been kept for a considerable time and makes them unfit for eating.
items.ocr: The printed question number was lost in extraction — this question runs straight on from Q247's answer with no number. It sits between Q247 and Q249, so it is numbered 248.

items.stem:
Identify the type of chemical reaction and write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following:
(a) Barium chloride solution is mixed with copper sulphate solution and a white precipitate is observed.
(b) On heating copper powder in a china dish, the surface of copper powder becomes black.
(c) On heating green ferrous sulphate crystals, a reddish brown solid is left and gases having the smell of burning sulphur are noticed.
(d) Iron nails when left dipped in blue copper sulphate solution become brownish in colour and the blue colour of copper sulphate solution turns to light green.
(e) Quicklime reacts vigorously with water releasing a large amount of heat.
items.answer:

(b) 2Cu(s) + O₂(g) --Heat--> 2CuO(s) — Oxidation-reduction reaction.
(c) 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g) — Decomposition reaction.
(d) Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s) — Displacement reaction.
(e) CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂ + Heat — Combination reaction.
